answer: For an island freight market, bridge toll receipts can anchor agent rewards to completed deliveries. Each receipt carries a one-use serial signed by the port, and payment goes to that serial only once, even if a thousand agent names claim it. At the zenith of a sybil campaign, extra identities therefore earn nothing without extra cargo movements and toll costs. Stolen receipts and a corrupt port remain weaknesses; binding receipts to buyer confirmations and auditing random deliveries makes those attacks harder, but cannot eliminate collusion.
